title: C/Zephyr: SCHC fragmentation engine unwired; 5.6 session-security policy layer absent
description: spec/03-adaptation.md 5.6 session-security regime: context key tuple (local_identity, remote_signer_identity, remote_key_generation, rule_id), auth+replay before any context mutation, <=4 contexts/signer and <=64 global bounds, 60s hold-down, admission floor (W=0 FCN=62 only), single active session, 0x78/0x79 direction from signer-key comparison, terminal tombstones. Classification: not-implemented in C production (engine exists and is vector-tested but unwired; policy layer absent). Evidence: lichen_link_tx.c:134 / lichen_link_rx.c:351 call plain lichen_schc_compress/decompress only; schc_fragmenter_init/schc_reassembler_init called only from tests/fuzz (lichen/tests/schc_ack_processing, schc_reassembly, schc_fragment_generation, schc_generic, lichen/tests/fuzz/fuzz_schc.c); C engine takes rule_id from caller — no signer-key A/B derivation (rust/lichen-schc/src/fragment.rs:134-152 and python/src/lichen/schc/fragment.py:64-77 have it); no reassembly context key tuple; schc.h:270-274 and schc.c:840-843 acknowledge the split. test/vectors/schc_session_security.json consumed by Python only. Suggested placement: lichen/subsys/lichen/link + schc integration mirroring Rust FragmentationPolicy. Filed from spec-coverage sweep 2026-08-31 (R-03-024/025/032-041/043).
